reviews.mechanism: Native model is lowered into an operator graph; compiler-style passes inject parallelism, optimization and analysis; each operator is routed among profiled, predicted and analytical backends with prioritized fallback; search proposes configurations over a versioned system description.
reviews.state_and_control_ownership: Versioned model graph, parallelism, hardware/topology, precision and runtime configuration own comparison identity. The simulator owns proposals and predictions. Real runtime traces and hardware replay own calibration and release acceptance.

evaluation_contract.memory_case: Qwen3-30B-A3B; 8 GPUs; FSDP=8; batch=2; sequence length=8192
evaluation_contract.serving_case: LLaMA-3 70B; NVIDIA Hopper; fixed output length; 100ms end-to-end latency SLO
evaluation_contract.claim_boundary: Reported errors and throughput improvements are author results for disclosed configurations, not a universal simulator guarantee.

tradeoffs_and_failures: Shared representation reduces drift but propagates common graph or calibration errors across training and inference.
Profiling backend is accurate but costly; prediction is faster but model-dependent; analytical backend is portable but weak for complex kernels.
Stale profile databases, unsupported operators, inaccurate overlap/congestion models and unsafe search pruning can produce a wrong Pareto frontier.
reviews.fallback: Use analytical/prediction results only for proposal; re-profile high-value configurations and require real-hardware replay/canary for release. Keep separate simulators or direct sweeps when scope is fixed or calibration is weak.

artifact.boundary: Do not claim public code, immutable commit or reproducibility.
